slides.title: Executive summary

paragraphs.text: Executive summary
Raise 2027 prices in mid-market and enterprise, stage SMB behind a stop rule, spare promotion customers
Churn is rising because of the 2025 promotion, not core price resistance
–	The promotion cohort drives about 94% of the SMB rise
–	Onboarding alone removes about a tenth of SMB churn
Pricing power sits in mid-market and enterprise, not yet in SMB
–	Retention: 112% mid-market, 118% enterprise, 94% SMB
–	Inkwell's $9 plan undercuts our $15; win rate fell to 38%
The CFO's 12% plan is worth about $7.6M in 2027, not $10.3M
–	Renewal dates and 7% enterprise caps cut the gain
–	A segmented plan keeps most of it, with less risk
A segmented plan adds about $5.6M and meets the 15% goal, with no cushion
–	The 8% SMB step nets only about $0.7M
–	Mid-market and enterprise move in January; SMB waits for a test

The step is small and close to break-even, so it needs a stop rule
▪	Break-even: the step stops paying if it lifts monthly SMB churn by more than about 0.6 percentage points through 2027 (8% ÷ 108% ÷ 12 months)
▪	Customers not from the promotion react as all SMB did in 2023; Inkwell's $9 plan did not exist then, so the response could be larger
▪	Lost customers are valued at the new price; any effect on new-customer win rates is not included
▪	The promotion cohort is left out of the step
1  Estimate by the team from the briefing pack; the live formula is in the Calculations sheet of the source workbook
Sources: Palisade Docs briefing pack (synthetic benchmark data); team analysis
